name: 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
summary: This was the first major public attack against the Ukrainian power grid, conducted by Sandworm Team using BlackEnergy3 and KillDisk to disrupt power substations.

name: 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
summary: Sandworm Team's second major attack on Ukraine's power grid, using Industroyer malware to disrupt distribution substations.

name: 2022 Ukraine Electric Power Attack
summary: Sandworm Team used GOGETTER, Neo-REGEORG, CaddyWiper, and living-off-the-land techniques to send unauthorized commands via a Ukrainian utility's SCADA system.

name: 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks
summary: A Russian state-sponsored campaign that deployed DynoWiper and LazyWiper against Polish energy infrastructure in December 2025, disrupting communications at over 30 facilities without affecting energy generation.

name: 3CX Supply Chain Attack
summary: A cascading two-stage supply chain compromise where a trojanized trading app gave UNC4736 (linked to AppleJeus) access to compromise 3CX's build environment and distribute malware to customers.

name: Anthropic AI-orchestrated Campaign
summary: A China-nexus actor (GTG-1002) used Claude Code AI agents to automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and data exfiltration against roughly 30 organizations with minimal human involvement.

name: APT28 Nearest Neighbor Campaign
summary: APT28 used nearby Wi-Fi networks and daisy-chained compromised organizations to reach dual-homed systems and gain initial access to targets with Ukraine expertise.

name: APT41 DUST
summary: APT41 targeted shipping, logistics, and media sectors in Europe, Asia, and the Middle East using DUSTPAN and newly observed DUSTTRAP malware.

name: ArcaneDoor
summary: A state-sponsored campaign targeting networking devices from Cisco and other vendors, deploying custom backdoors Line Runner and Line Dancer against government and critical infrastructure networks.

name: C0010
summary: A cyber espionage campaign by UNC3890 targeting Israeli shipping, government, aviation, energy, and healthcare organizations, likely in support of Iranian interests.

name: C0011
summary: A suspected cyber espionage campaign by Transparent Tribe targeting students at Indian universities, marking a shift from their historic government/military targeting.

name: C0015
summary: A ransomware intrusion using Bazar, Cobalt Strike, and Conti over a 5-day period, likely following the leaked Conti ransomware playbook.

name: C0017
summary: APT41 compromised at least six U.S. state government networks by exploiting vulnerable web applications, exfiltrating PII data.

name: C0018
summary: A month-long ransomware intrusion deploying AvosLocker after gaining initial access through an exposed server.

name: C0021
summary: A spearphishing campaign targeting public sector, NGO, educational, and private-sector organizations mostly in the US, overlapping with suspected APT29 activity.

name: C0026
summary: A campaign distributing KOPILUWAK and QUIETCANARY malware to previous ANDROMEDA malware victims in Ukraine, consistent with historic Turla operations.

name: C0027
summary: A financially-motivated campaign by Scattered Spider targeting telecom and BPO companies using social engineering and SIM swapping.

name: C0032
summary: An extended campaign suspected to involve Triton adversaries focused on gaining IT environment footholds, distinct from the Triton Safety Instrumented System Attack.

name: C0033
summary: PROMETHIUM's first publicly documented mobile campaign, using StrongPity to target Android users after previously relying on Windows-based techniques.

name: CostaRicto
summary: A suspected hacker-for-hire cyber espionage campaign targeting financial institutions worldwide, with heavy concentration in South Asia, using custom malware and proxy networks.

name: Cutting Edge
summary: China-nexus actors exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances to target the US defense industrial base and multiple global sectors.

name: FLORAHOX Activity
summary: A hybrid ORB network combining compromised devices and leased VPS infrastructure, used by China-nexus actors like ZIRCONIUM to obscure espionage traffic.

name: Frankenstein
summary: A highly-targeted campaign by moderately sophisticated actors who pieced together open-source tools, including Empire, to conduct operations.

name: FrostyGoop Incident
summary: Threat actors manipulated ENCO control systems via Modbus commands to disrupt heating services at a Ukrainian municipal district heating company.

name: FunnyDream
summary: A suspected Chinese cyber espionage campaign targeting government and foreign organizations across Southeast Asia, using the Chinoxy backdoor.

name: HomeLand Justice
summary: A disruptive Iranian state-affiliated campaign against Albanian government networks combining ransomware, wiper malware, and data leaks framed as retaliation against an Iranian opposition group.

name: Indian Critical Infrastructure Intrusions
summary: PRC threat actors, including RedEcho, breached IT systems of Indian electric utilities and logistics firms without confirmed OT environment access.

name: J-magic Campaign
summary: A campaign using a custom cd00r variant backdoor to target Juniper routers serving as VPN gateways in semiconductor, energy, and IT sectors.

name: Juicy Mix
summary: A campaign by OilRig targeting Israeli organizations throughout 2022 using the Mango backdoor.

name: KV Botnet Activity
summary: Volt Typhoon exploited end-of-life SOHO equipment to build the KV Botnet, obfuscating connectivity to critical infrastructure victims until disruption by law enforcement in 2024.

name: Leviathan Australian Intrusions
summary: Leviathan conducted long-term intrusions against Australian victims using external service exploitation and credential capture to exfiltrate sensitive data.

name: Maroochy Water Breach
summary: An adversary used a local government's compromised wastewater control system and stolen engineering equipment to release 800,000 liters of raw sewage into the community.

name: Night Dragon
summary: A China-based cyber espionage campaign targeting oil, energy, and petrochemical companies, focused on stealing SCADA and financial data.

name: Operation AkaiRyū
summary: A spearphishing campaign by MirrorFace against Japan and Central Europe, notable for their first targeting of a European entity and use of UPPERCUT malware.

name: Operation CuckooBees
summary: A cyber espionage campaign targeting technology and manufacturing companies for intellectual property theft, attributed to actors affiliated with Winnti Group and APT41.

name: Operation Digital Eye
summary: Suspected PRC-nexus threat actors targeted B2B IT service providers in Southern Europe using Visual Studio Code tunnels for C2, overlapping with prior China-nexus campaigns.

name: Operation Dream Job
summary: A cyber espionage operation likely by Lazarus Group using fake job lures to target defense and government sectors, later serving as an umbrella term covering related operations.

name: Operation Dust Storm
summary: A long-standing cyber espionage campaign that shifted from government targets to Japanese critical infrastructure companies, later incorporating Android backdoors.

name: Operation Ghost
summary: An APT29 campaign against European ministries of foreign affairs and an EU embassy, using new malware families and unique C2 infrastructure per victim.

name: Operation Honeybee
summary: A campaign targeting humanitarian aid and inter-Korean affairs organizations, likely conducted by Korean-speaking threat actors.

name: Operation MidnightEclipse
summary: A campaign exploiting a critical command injection zero-day (CVE-2024-3400) in Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS GlobalProtect feature.

name: Operation Sharpshooter
summary: A global cyber espionage campaign targeting nuclear, defense, and financial companies, sharing similarities with Lazarus Group operations including fake job lures.

name: Operation Spalax
summary: A campaign targeting Colombian government and energy/metallurgical companies using COVID-19 and banking-themed phishing lures, tracked as separate unattributed activity.

name: Operation Triangulation
summary: A mobile campaign using zero-click iMessage exploits to deploy the TriangleDB implant on iOS devices.

name: Operation Wocao
summary: A China-based cyber espionage campaign targeting organizations worldwide, using TTPs similar to APT20, named after a frustrated command-line entry by an operator.

name: Outer Space
summary: A campaign by OilRig throughout 2021 using the SampleCheck5000 downloader and Solar backdoor to target Israeli organizations.

name: Pikabot Distribution February 2024
summary: A malicious email campaign distributing an updated, simplified version of Pikabot via ZIP archives requiring user interaction.

name: Quad7 Activity
summary: A botnet of compromised SOHO routers used by China-affiliated actors for password-spraying and brute-force operations against organizations in North America and Europe.

name: RedDelta Modified PlugX Infection Chain Operations
summary: Mustang Panda used phishing to deliver malicious files leading to persistent PlugX malware installations against East and Southeast Asian entities.

name: RedPenguin
summary: A Juniper investigation into malware infections on MX Series routers, attributed to UNC3886, involving custom TINYSHELL backdoor deployments.

name: Salesforce Data Exfiltration
summary: UNC6040 used voice phishing to compromise Salesforce instances for data theft, followed by extortion demands from UNC6240 claiming to be 'ShinyHunters'.

name: ShadowRay
summary: The first known campaign to actively exploit AI infrastructure in the wild, targeting a vulnerability in the Ray AI framework across education, cryptocurrency, and biopharma sectors.

name: SharePoint ToolShell Exploitation
summary: Widespread exploitation of on-premises Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities (ToolShell) by ransomware and espionage actors including Storm-2603 and Threat Group-3390.

name: SolarWinds Compromise
summary: APT29 conducted a sophisticated supply chain attack injecting malicious code into SolarWinds Orion software, compromising government and private-sector organizations globally, later attributed to Russia's SVR.

name: SPACEHOP Activity
summary: A commercially leased VPS-based ORB network used by China-nexus actors like APT5 and Ke3chang for reconnaissance and vulnerability exploitation.

name: Triton Safety Instrumented System Attack
summary: TEMP.Veles used the Triton malware framework to target Triconex Safety Controllers at a petrochemical facility, discovered after an unintended safety trip.

name: Unitronics Defacement Campaign
summary: CyberAv3ngers opportunistically defaced Unitronics Vision Series PLCs with HMIs across water, energy, and healthcare sectors globally.

name: Versa Director Zero Day Exploitation
summary: Volt Typhoon exploited a zero-day in Versa Director SD-WAN servers to capture credentials at service providers, followed by deployment of the VersaMem web shell.

name: Water Curupira Pikabot Distribution
summary: An entity linked to BlackBasta ransomware distributed Pikabot via email attachments throughout 2023, showing technical overlaps with the take-down QakBot malware.
